question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 8 & -6\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -60 \\ -60 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 8 \\ 3 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 8 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 8 \\ 3 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 8 \\ 3 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 8 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 8 \\ 3 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 12 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}80 & -60 \\ -60 & 45\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=80+45+6=131.
$$
